standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism and its triangle
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone C(f) of a map of dg modules with its inclusion, projection and the triangle it forms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The triangles and their cones are the objects of the morphism (a, b, c) (source lines 1019-1026).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy equivalence and inverse in the homotopy category
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is a homotopy equivalence when it has an inverse in the homotopy category of dg modules.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis gives inverses a^{-1} and b^{-1}, and the conclusion is that c has one (source lines 1027, 1031-1034, 1060-1061).

standard_prerequisites.name: Functoriality of the cone and nilpotence of a composite
standard_prerequisites.statement: A homotopy commutative square induces a map of the cones, and a composite of two compatible maps of admissible sequences is homotopic to zero (the author's lemmas lemma-functorial-cone and lemma-nilpotent, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: The first builds c'; the second shows that the composites of c and c' have square zero, which is what makes 2 - c an inverse (source lines 1035, 1056-1061).

core_obligations: Build the candidate inverse: choose homotopy inverses a^{-1} and b^{-1} of a and b, and apply the functoriality of the cone to the resulting homotopy commutative square to obtain c' : C(f_2) -> C(f_1) (source lines 1031-1035).

Show the composites have square zero: using that the two squares of the resulting diagram commute up to homotopy and that its rows are admissible short exact sequences, invoke the nilpotence result to get (c - 1)^2 = 0 in the homotopy category (source lines 1036-1059).
Conclude the inverse: deduce that c is an isomorphism in the homotopy category with inverse 2 - c, so c is a homotopy equivalence (source lines 1060-1061).

proof_roadmap.step: Take homotopy inverses of a and b and build c' from the functoriality of the cone.
Show the composites have square zero using the nilpotence result.
Conclude that c is an isomorphism with inverse 2 - c.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-third-isomorphism at source lines 1015-1028: for a dg algebra A and a morphism (a, b, c) of the triangles built from two maps f_1 and f_2 of dg A-modules, if a and b are homotopy equivalences then so is c. The proof at source lines 1030-1062 has to manufacture the inverse of c and then verify it. It picks homotopy inverses a^{-1} and b^{-1} for a and b in the homotopy category, uses the author's functoriality of the cone to build a map c' : C(f_2) -> C(f_1) out of them, and then must show that c' is an inverse of c up to homotopy. The verification is where the work is: the composites c' c and c c' are shown to have square zero in the homotopy category by exhibiting the commutativity-up-to-homotopy of a three-term diagram whose rows are admissible short exact sequences and invoking the author's nilpotence result, after which the explicit inverse 2 - c is read off. The statement records only the conclusion. The two invoked author results are retained alongside so their references resolve inside the package.
